# ECN-2026-034 Change notice - Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01

Reason for change
- Update to documented maximum workpiece envelope for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to align machine control limits and shop tooling constraints. The maximum ring outer diameter for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01) is 1240 mm. This change corrects discrepancies between operator reference sheets and machine parameter screens and reduces risk of out-of-tolerance rolling events and tooling interference.

Affected items
- Equipment setup sheets and planning templates for EQ-P1-L1-RR01.
- Job traveler entries and nest planning documents used on P1-L1.
- Operator work instructions that reference allowable ring outer diameter for rolling operations.
- Downstream handling fixtures sized to receive rings from EQ-P1-L1-RR01.

Implementation
- Update master setup sheet for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 to show the maximum ring outer diameter as 1240 mm and distribute controlled copies to the P1-L1 shift leads.  
- Revise SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-05 references in procedure cross‑lists to point operators to the corrected envelope value; coordinate updates with the document control team.  
- Validate change by performing a no-load dry run with standard handling fixtures to confirm clearances and interlocks; document results on the equipment checklist and attach to the updated setup sheet.  
- Communicate change to production planning and scheduling to ensure invoices and quotes reflect the corrected capability.  
- Reference SB-1025 for safe blocking and support practices during setup and follow its restraint guidance when confirming outer diameter limits.

Approvals
- Engineering change owner signs for technical verification and release.  
- Maintenance signs for mechanical verification and fitment checks.  
- Operations signs for procedure acceptance and operator training acknowledgment.  
- Document control issues the updated controlled copies after approvals and archives prior versions per retention practice.
